atlanta-ga.work: As of November 21, 2026, doctors on this list are listed at Emory, Northside and Grady hospitals, and at 9 other practices across the metro, from Marietta to Stockbridge.
atlanta-ga.plan_line: Your plan may differ. Employer self-funded plans and Medicare Advantage plans can set their own rules. Check with your plan.

insurers.name: Anthem (Georgia's Blue Cross plan)
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: heavy bleeding, or pelvic pain, pressure or passing urine often, when not caused by infection.

insurers.name: UnitedHealthcare
insurers.policy: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding and Uterine Fibroids (2026T0442WW), in effect November 1, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids that cause symptoms; the detailed rules are not public. Not covered when the purpose is to preserve the ability to have children.

insurers.name: Aetna
insurers.policy: Clinical Policy Bulletin 0304, last reviewed April 17, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: as an alternative to surgery to remove the uterus or the fibroids, when heavy periods, pain or pressure, urinary symptoms or pain with sex persist.

insurers.name: Cigna
insurers.policy: EviCore Peripheral Vascular Intervention Guidelines V2.0.2026, in effect November 5, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids seen on an earlier ultrasound or MRI, plus abnormal bleeding, period pain, pain with sex or urinary symptoms.

insurers.name: Humana Medicare Advantage
insurers.policy: Uterine Fibroid Surgical Treatments (HUM-1231-005), in effect April 1, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids confirmed, you want to keep your uterus, and symptoms for 3 months or more despite medical treatment where that is appropriate.

insurers.name: Medicare (Original)
insurers.policy: National decision 20.28, Therapeutic Embolization, dated December 15, 1978
insurers.says: No specific policy; decided case by case.

atlanta-ga.medicaid_intro: Georgia Medicaid plans today are Amerigroup, CareSource and Peach State (contracts run through June 2027; the plans may change after that). We found no written policy on fibroid embolization from any of them.

medicaid.name: Peach State
medicaid.policy: Medicaid prior authorization list, effective December 31, 2025

medicaid.name: CareSource
medicaid.says: Not on its list of procedures that need approval, for doctors in its network.

medicaid.name: Amerigroup
medicaid.says: No public answer. Ask the plan.

medicaid.name: State Medicaid (no plan)
medicaid.says: Not on its list of procedures that need approval.

atlanta-ga.lead: Most large insurers in Georgia cover fibroid embolization when certain conditions are met. Medicaid rules differ by plan.
steps: Find your plan in the tables below.
Call the number on your insurance card. Ask whether fibroid embolization (UFE) is covered for you, and whether you need approval before the procedure.
Ask the doctor's office to check with your plan before you book.
